summary.headline: Subex Q2 FY27 revenue rose 7.7% QoQ to INR 85.59 crore (+24% YoY), with normalized EBITDA of INR 17.77 crore and a fifth straight QoQ growth quarter.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 7.7% QoQ to INR 85.59 crore from INR 79.45 crore, marking five consecutive quarters of QoQ growth per management. Normalized EBITDA rose to INR 17.77 crore from INR 16.87 crore despite the annual wage increase, while normalized PAT fell to INR 14.3 crore from INR 16.9 crore; reported PAT was INR 14.29 crore versus INR 14.22 crore. Cash and equivalents rose to INR 198 crore from INR 184 crore. Management spent most of the call on a strategic repositioning toward AI-led "integrity of decisions" and economic integrity, while declining to give quantitative guidance.

segments.name: India revenue
segments.commentary: About 3% of total revenue, up from about 2%. Management does not expect a meaningful uptick, citing Reliance Jio building its own stack; Vodafone is the existing India customer.

segments.name: Managed services
segments.commentary: Covers maintenance, upgrades and upsells on Subex's own products only. Management says it is being made more efficient through AI agents rather than shrinking.

segments.name: Partner Ecosystem Management (PEM)
segments.commentary: Legacy product being modernized with new features; management calls it a historical profitability generator. Competitor consolidation has opened opportunities, and several recently announced deals were in this product.

guidance_outlook: No formal quantitative guidance. Aspiration is high single-digit to double-digit growth; management says it expects roughly 14-15% growth over the next year, which it calls no small feat.
EBITDA path to continue in the same way; management wants margins durable within a range, though they will not be the same every quarter.
No major challenges to order execution. Middle East tensions and US elections are wildcards; management expects no change for the next two quarters absent a black swan event.
Cash to be used primarily for inorganic growth opportunities, with an acquisition pipeline being actively run.
Buyback not possible now because of negative retained earnings. ESOP trust share purchases to be executed in Q3 FY27, spaced out, and only when no UPSI is on hand.
capex_capacity: R&D is expensed through the P&L and not capitalized, so it does not draw on the balance sheet cash.
AI SDLC lifted core engineering throughput: sprints of about 14-15 features against a plan of 10 per quarter, per management. Management says benchmarks have not yet been reached.

HyperSense implementations are being deployed about 15-20% faster than timelines promised to customers. The Library of Controls (ROC) is at an earlier stage and is being built product stack by product stack.
demand_pricing: Business is backlog-driven: about 70% of each year's revenue is recurring or carried over, and the rest comes from new orders won in the year.

Per management, roughly 40-50% of a new deal's value is recognized in the first four quarters, with the balance straight-lined after go-live via MS or AMC payments. Licence is taken upfront and recognized during implementation.
Three POCs closed technically in the quarter (Architecture of Autonomy, agents, social engineering use cases), with three more completed. The sales team is now converting them to commercial deals.

A new AI agent squad deal closed in 90 days from first pitch. The agents build on MicroPro for detection-to-investigation workflows, and management says they are scalable to 50,000 transactions with auditability. Commercial conversations are under way with several customers.
Management says the telco industry grows about 2-3%, and Subex is growing 3-5x that rate. Management estimates the INR depreciation benefit at about 2-3% QoQ and 8-10% YoY, and says QoQ it was flat.
Management defines its TAM as INR/USD 4.3 billion (as stated in the investor presentation).

qa_highlights.question: If AI lets operators run fraud and assurance in-house, what replaces managed services revenue over two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said managed services will not be replaced. Subex's managed services cover only its own products and it works across hundreds of telcos, which gives cross-telco fraud visibility. Delivery is being made more efficient with AI agents.

qa_highlights.question: Can management give quantitative guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give formal guidance. It said the aspiration is high single-digit to double-digit growth, with a 14-15% growth delivery in the next year called no small feat, and margins to stay durable.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the YoY growth is constant currency, given INR depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR depreciation benefits Subex by about 2-3% QoQ and 8-10% YoY. QoQ it was flat.

qa_highlights.question: How will the ~INR 200 crore cash be used, and is a buyback possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Primary use is inorganic growth, with a pipeline under active review. A buyback is not possible now because retained earnings are negative. R&D is expensed, so it does not use the balance sheet.

qa_highlights.question: Has time from deal signing to go-live shortened from 45 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says HyperSense deployments are running about 15-20% faster than promised timelines. The Library of Controls is less advanced. AI SDLC is raising engineering throughput but has not hit benchmarks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AI agent squad, and is it scalable and in demand?
qa_highlights.answer: The agents are multi-agent, with manager and router agents, and are scalable to 50,000 transactions with repeatable auditability. The deal is with a different customer from the earlier GPU-constrained one. Management says it has pitched widely and is in commercial talks with several customers.

risks_watch: Net profit fell QoQ (normalized PAT INR 14.3 crore vs INR 16.9 crore) even though EBITDA rose; watch the gap between EBITDA and PAT.
Dependence on converting POCs and the AI agent squad deal into recurring commercial revenue; management has not disclosed revenue for these.
Negative retained earnings block buybacks; watch the trust's ESOP share purchases in Q3 FY27.
Growth is partly INR-driven (8-10% YoY benefit per management), so constant-currency growth is lower than reported.
Management's strategic pivot toward AI-led decision integrity is a direction, not yet an established market position; management says the core business must scale first.
Middle East and US election geopolitical risks, and the Jio in-house stack reducing India opportunity.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the operating turnaround and on the AI agent deal wins, but deliberately cautious on forward numbers: it declined quantitative guidance and framed the AI strategy as aspirational rather than established. Management was candid about gaps (AI SDLC benchmarks not yet met, ROC less advanced, India not growing) and admitted that the HyperSense time-to-live window is still not where it needs to be.

If there's one thing I'd want you to remember, it's that. my goal is not to build a better version of the Subex of yesterday.
In any given year whatever revenue numbers that you see, 70% of it is recurring or backlogged.

growth.why: Management declined formal quantitative guidance but said it expects roughly 14-15% growth over the next year, backed partly by a ~70% recurring/carried-over revenue base, POC conversions and a new AI agent deal, with no specific capacity additions cited.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin was 20.8% (INR 17.77 crore on INR 85.59 crore) and management wants margins durable within a range, but normalized PAT fell to INR 14.3 crore from INR 16.9 crore and no expansion target was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects roughly 14-15% growth over the next year, backed by about 70% recurring or carried-over revenue, POC conversions and a new AI agent squad deal, though no quantitative guidance was formally given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: R&D is expensed and not capitalized, and no capex, plant or utilisation figures were discussed, so there is no sign of a capex announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined formal quantitative guidance and held its high single-digit to double-digit aspiration, so no upgrade is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management sees no major challenges to order execution and expects no change for the next two quarters absent a black swan event, though Middle East and US election risks remain.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The AI agent squad built on MicroPro is scalable to 50,000 transactions, three POCs have closed technically and commercial talks are under way, but no launch date was given and the PEM modernization is ongoing.

rows.label: AI agent squad and POC conversions to commercial deals
rows.why: Three POCs closed technically with three more completed, and a new AI agent squad deal closed in 90 days, but management has not disclosed revenue for these and conversion is still in progress.

rows.label: HyperSense deployments faster than promised timelines
rows.why: Deployments run about 15-20% faster than customer-promised timelines, though management admits the time-to-live window is still not where it needs to be.

rows.label: ESOP trust share purchases
rows.why: Buyback is blocked by negative retained earnings, so the trust will buy shares in Q3 FY27 spaced out and only when no UPSI is held.

tone.note: Management was confident on the turnaround and the AI agent deal wins but cautious on forward numbers, declining quantitative guidance and calling the AI pivot aspirational; analysts pressed on managed services durability, constant-currency growth and the cash use.
